Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re evaluating the residency/KMS onboarding work and need clarity on how Redwood expects to bill the one-time transition/setup fee for data residency (migration, HSM provisioning, auditlog pipelines). Specifically:

- Do you invoice that as a single up-front charge, or can it be amortized across the committed term?
- If amortized, what are the typical term options (12/24/36 months) and how does that appear on the monthly invoice?
- Can the cost be split between the compliance add-on and the Dedicated capacity commit? We’d prefer not to treat it as pure operating spend.

For budget planning we need an example showing the $120,000 engineering/setup fee split across a 24-month term vs an upfront invoice, and the net impact to our committed monthly charge. Can you send a couple of scenarios and indicate any discount or crediting approaches you’d recommend?

Also let me know what you need from procurement to issue a PO.

Thanks,
Linda Park
Chief Security Officer
MedusaCare

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers first, then I’ll loop Ben for the spreadsheets: 

- We support both approaches: a one-time up-front invoice or an amortized spread across the committed term (your choice).
- Common amortization windows are 12/24/36 months; we typically align amortization with the customer committed term to avoid mid-contract accounting mismatches.
- Splitting between a compliance add-on and reserved capacity is possible — we model that as an allocation line on the invoice (x% to compliance add-on, y% to reserved capacity). It does not change the total economics, but it may help your internal chargeback.

Recommendation: for deals with multi-year commit we usually amortize over the commit length (24 months in your case) so the monthly view is predictable for finance. Ben has prepared two scenarios (attached):

Scenario 1 — Amortize $120,000 over 24 months: 
  • $5,000/mo amortization line (separately billed under “Compliance Onboarding”).
  • Core committed monthly price remains unchanged; the $5k shows as a compliance line item.

Scenario 2 — One-time invoice $120,000 up front: 
  • One invoice at signature.
  • We can offer a trade: take the one-time up-front and we’ll apply a one-time credit of 10% to the first 6 months of committed capacity (this is an optional concession).

I’ve asked Ben to attach the workbook with numeric breakdowns and a simple flow diagram that shows where the charge lands on the invoice and how it is apportioned. If you want, we can also model a hybrid (50/50 split between add-on and commit).

Next step: Ben will drop the workbook. If that looks good, I can generate a draft SOW and an estimated invoice for PO submission.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Linda — attaching the workbook and a simple diagram. Summary of the two modeled options (numbers in workbook):

Scenario A — 24-month amortization (recommended for commit alignment)
  • One-time onboarding: $120,000
  • Amortization period: 24 months
  • Monthly amortization line: $5,000/month billed as “Compliance Onboarding (amortized)”.
  • Net monthly invoice first 24 months = committed capacity + $5,000 compliance line.
  • If you want the cost split, default allocation used in workbook: 60% to Compliance Add-on, 40% to Dedicated capacity (you can tweak).

Scenario B — Up-front invoice with short-term credit
  • One-time onboarding: $120,000 due at signature
  • One-time concession: 10% credit applied to committed capacity invoices across months 1–6 (spread as negative line item).
  • Effective short-term discount shown in workbook for month 1–6 only.

Other notes:
  • Tax and invoice timing: onboarding invoice can be issued net-30 or net-45 depending on procurement preference.
  • Accounting classification: if you treat onboarding as CapEx vs OpEx, we can provide a memo describing allocation for your finance team.
